news.text: 5 March saw NASA scientists announce that the orbiting **Lunar Prospector** spacecraft had detected compelling evidence of water ice buried at the Moon's polar craters. Using a neutron spectrometer to peer into permanently frozen shadows, the probe identified significant hydrogen signatures that suggested frozen reservoirs beneath the lunar dust. Space enthusiasts excitedly celebrated the prospect of future moon bases brewing their own tea, though engineers cautioned that mining frozen regolith remained somewhat challenging.

news.text: 15 March saw American hip-hop veterans **Run-D.M.C.** and dance producer Jason Nevins claim number one on the UK singles chart with their pulsating remix of *It's Like That*. The breakbeat revival of the 1983 rap classic proved so dominant that it kept the Spice Girls' retro Motown homage *Stop* firmly stuck at number two, ending their record run of six consecutive debut number ones. Pop pundits proclaimed the death of bubblegum pop, blissfully unaware that girl groups were merely catching their breath.

news.text: 23 March saw *Titanic* conquer the **70th Academy Awards** at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, matching the historic benchmark of eleven Oscar statuettes set by *Ben-Hur*. Taking the stage to collect Best Director, Canadian filmmaker **James Cameron** famously quoted his own screenplay by shouting to the star-studded audience that he was the king of the world. While Hollywood rivals cringed into their champagne flutes at his unchecked hubris, Cameron was entirely too busy counting his billions to notice.
news.youtube: James Cameron Im the king of the world Oscar speech 1998

news.text: 24 March saw the European Commission confirm that eleven European Union countries had successfully met the economic criteria to launch the **Euro** single currency in January 1999. While France and Germany toasted the historic step toward continent-wide integration, the United Kingdom pointedly remained on the sidelines under its hard-won opt-out clause. Fleet Street tabloids breathed a collective sigh of relief that the British sovereign, and more importantly the portrait of Her Majesty, would not yet be exchanged for European banknotes.

29 March saw **"Stone Cold" Steve Austin** defeat Shawn Michaels at *WrestleMania XIV* in Boston to win his first WWF World Heavyweight Championship, ushering in the peak of the Attitude Era. Special outside enforcer **Mike Tyson** turned on D-Generation X to count the winning three-fall, subsequently decking Michaels with a vicious right hand when the former champion protested. Michaels departed the ring to nurse severe back injuries that would keep him retired for four years, leaving Austin in undisputed possession of the company.

news.text: 31 March saw Blizzard Entertainment release real-time strategy powerhouse *StarCraft* for Windows PCs, sparking an electronic sports revolution that would grip millions. Pitting the militaristic Terrans, biomechanical Zerg, and psionic Protoss against one another in an unforgiving space opera, its razor-sharp faction balance transformed strategy gaming from a relaxed pastime into an intense test of actions-per-minute. Within months, South Korean internet cafés were packed with teenage tacticians forgoing sleep to master the dreaded six-pool Zergling rush.
